question_html: What is the primary function of final accounts (Trading Account, Profit and Loss Account, and Balance Sheet) for a business entity?

options.A: To calculate the personal income tax liability of the proprietor
options.B: To exhibit truly and fairly the performance and the financial position of the business
options.C: To maintain chronological records of daily cash transactions
options.D: To determine the exact market value of the business for sale

answer_html: Answer: (B) The principal function of final accounts is to exhibit truly and fairly the performance and the financial position of the business[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes between the Income Statement and the Position Statement?

options.A: Income statement exhibits assets and liabilities as at the close of the financial year, while position statement discloses net profit or loss.
options.B: Income statement discloses net profit or net loss, while position statement exhibits assets and liabilities as at the close of the financial year.
options.C: Income statement is prepared only for corporate entities, while position statement is for non-corporate entities.
options.D: Income statement is a statement of cash flows, while position statement is a trial balance.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Income statement discloses net profit or net loss after adjusting expenditures from income earned, whereas position statement exhibits assets and liabilities as at a particular date[cite: 17].

question_html: According to the basic principles in regard to the accumulation of accounting period data, which of the following is required?

options.A: No distinction should be made between capital and revenue receipts.
options.B: Income and expenses relating to one period of account should be mixed with another.
options.C: A distinction should be made between capital and revenue receipts and payments.
options.D: Personal income and expenditure should be combined with business income.

answer_html: Answer: (C) One of the basic principles is that a distinction should be made between capital and revenue receipts and payments[cite: 17].

question_html: Which accounting principle demands that expenses incurred to earn revenue should be properly matched with the revenues of the period?

options.A: Consistency Principle
options.B: Matching Principle
options.C: Materiality Principle
options.D: Conservatism Principle

answer_html: Answer: (B) The principle that governs the concept of matching expenses incurred to earn revenue is called the Matching Principle[cite: 17].

question_html: How should income received in advance be treated in the financial statements?

options.A: Credited to the current year's Profit and Loss Account
options.B: Shown on the assets side of the Balance Sheet
options.C: Shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet as 'income received in advance'
options.D: Ignored until the next financial year

answer_html: Answer: (C) Income received in advance should be shown in the Balance Sheet on the liabilities side and credited to the Profit and Loss Account of the next year[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the valuation principle for closing inventory according to accounting standards?

options.A: Historical cost only
options.B: Net realizable value only
options.C: Cost or net realizable value whichever is higher
options.D: Cost or net realizable value whichever is lower

answer_html: Answer: (D) The valuation principle for closing inventory is cost or net realizable value whichever is lower[cite: 17].

question_html: If closing stock appears in the trial balance, how is it treated?

options.A: It is entered on the credit side of the Trading Account and asset side of Balance Sheet.
options.B: It is not entered in the trading account and is shown only in the balance sheet.
options.C: It is deducted from purchases in the Trading Account and omitted from the Balance Sheet.
options.D: It is added to opening stock.

answer_html: Answer: (B) If closing stock appears in the Trial Balance, it is not entered in the trading account; it is shown only in the balance sheet because it has already been adjusted to arrive at Cost of Goods Sold[cite: 17].

question_html: In the case of a sole proprietorship, how is income tax paid treated?

options.A: Debited to Profit and Loss Account like other business expenses
options.B: Treated as an operating expense
options.C: Debited to the Capital Account as a personal expense
options.D: Shown as a current liability in the Balance Sheet

answer_html: Answer: (C) In the case of sole proprietorship, income tax is treated as a personal expense and is debited to the Capital Account, not to the Profit and Loss Account[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the key difference between trade discount and cash discount regarding financial statements?

options.A: Trade discount is debited to P&L account, while cash discount is deducted from invoice.
options.B: Trade discount is not debited to P&L account because it is already adjusted in sales/purchases, whereas cash discount is debited/credited to P&L account.
options.C: Both trade discount and cash discount are debited to the Trading Account.
options.D: Neither discount is recorded in the books of accounts.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Trade discount is deducted from the invoice and not debited to P&L account, while cash discount is recorded and debited/credited to the Profit and Loss Account[cite: 17].

question_html: When bad debts are recovered after being written off, how should the recovered amount be treated?

options.A: Credited to the debtor's personal account
options.B: Credited to the Bad Debts Recovered Account as a gain (income)
options.C: Credited to the Capital Account directly
options.D: Credited to Sales Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) If a bad debt is recovered, it should not be credited to the party; it should be credited to Bad Debts Recovered Account and entered in the Profit and Loss Account on the credit side[cite: 17].

question_html: How is provision for discount on debtors calculated?

options.A: Calculated on total gross debtors without any deduction
options.B: Calculated after deducting the provision for doubtful debts from the total trade receivables
options.C: Calculated after adding total trade payables to debtors
options.D: Calculated as a percentage of total sales

answer_html: Answer: (B) The amount of provision for discount is calculated after deducting the provision for Bad Debts from the total trade receivables because provision for discount is created only on good debtors[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the distinction between provisions and reserves according to accounting principles?

options.A: Provisions are an appropriation of profits, while reserves are a charge against profits.
options.B: Provisions are a charge against profits, while reserves are an appropriation of profits.
options.C: Both provisions and reserves are charges against profits.
options.D: Both provisions and reserves are appropriations of profits.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Provisions are a charge against profits, whereas reserves are an appropriation of profits[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following is considered a limitation of financial statements?

options.A: They reflect exact current market values of all fixed assets.
options.B: They fully capture qualitative elements such as employee loyalty and calibre.
options.C: They are prepared on historical cost, ignoring subsequent changes in the value of money.
options.D: They are completely objective with no scope for accounting policies or estimates.

answer_html: Answer: (C) One of the principal limitations of financial statements is that they are prepared on the basis of historical cost, ignoring subsequent changes in the value of money[cite: 17].

question_html: When goods are sent to a customer on sale or return or approval basis and remain unapproved at the end of the year, how should the unapproved sale be treated?

options.A: Treat it as an actual completed sale and leave trade receivables unchanged.
options.B: Reverse the sale entry and include the goods in closing stock at cost price.
options.C: Ignore the transaction entirely as if it never occurred.
options.D: Debit purchases and credit sales.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Goods sent on approval should not be treated as actual sale till approved; the sale entry must be reversed and goods included in closing stock at cost price[cite: 17].

question_html: What does the term 'Reserve Fund' signify?

options.A: Profits kept in reserve and invested outside the business in readily realizable securities
options.B: A provision for doubtful debts maintained in liquid cash
options.C: Undistributed losses carried forward
options.D: Short-term bank overdraft facilities

answer_html: Answer: (A) Reserve Fund signifies the amount standing to the credit of reserve that is invested outside the business in securities which are readily realizable[cite: 17].

question_html: If sales revenue is ₹4,00,000, cost of goods sold is ₹3,10,000, and operating expenses are ₹60,000, what is the gross profit?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Gross profit is the difference between sales and cost of goods sold ($4,00,000 - 3,10,000 = ext{₹}90,000$)[cite: 17].

question_html: A company wishes to earn a 20% profit margin on selling price. Which of the following is the profit mark-up on cost which will achieve the required profit margin?
answer_html: Answer: (B) If margin is 20% of selling price (i.e. 20/100 or 1/5 of SP), then cost is 4 parts, so mark-up on cost is $1/4 = 25\%$[cite: 17].

question_html: If sales is ₹2,000 and the rate of gross profit on cost of goods sold is 25%, what will be the cost of goods sold?
answer_html: Answer: (C) If GP is 25% on cost ($1/4$ of cost), let cost = $100x$, Sales = $125x = 2,000$, so $x = 16$. Cost of goods sold = $100 imes 16 = ext{₹}1,600$[cite: 17].

question_html: Sales for the year ended 31st March, 2022 amounted to ₹10,00,000. Sales included goods sold to Mr. A for ₹50,000 at a profit of 20% on cost. Such goods are still lying in the godown at the buyer's risk. Therefore, such goods should be treated as part of:

options.A: Closing Inventory (at cost)
options.B: Goods in transit
options.C: Sales only, with no inventory adjustment
options.D: Purchases

answer_html: Answer: (A) Since goods are lying in the godown and sale is complete/at buyer's risk or considered as part of closing inventory depending on terms, wait—let's check MCQ 11 in text: such goods are treated as part of closing inventory/sales depending on the exact context. Actually, let's verify MCQ 11 answer from text: Answer (a) Sales (Wait, let's check text MCQ 11 hint: MCQ 11 answer is (a) Sales in the text key, but let's look at the options in the text). In text: (11) Sales for the year ended 31st March, 2022 amounted to 10,00,000... Answer key says: 11. (a)[cite: 17].

question_html: On 1st April 2021, provision for Doubtful Debts existed at ₹40,000. Trade receivables on 31.03.2022 were ₹15,00,000; bad debts totaled ₹1,00,000. If a provision equal to 5% of trade receivables is required, what amount is debited to the Profit and Loss Account?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Debtors after bad debts = $15,000,000 - 1,00,000 = 14,00,000$. Required provision = 5% of 14,00,000 = ₹70,000. Total required = Bad debts ($1,00,000) + New Provision ($70,000) - Opening Provision ($40,000) = ₹1,30,000[cite: 17].

question_html: Goods worth ₹6,000 are destroyed by fire and the insurance company admits a claim for ₹4,500. What is the net amount debited to the Profit and Loss Account?
answer_html: Answer: (C) The portion of loss not compensated by the insurance company ($6,000 - 4,500 = ext{₹}1,500$) is debited to the Profit and Loss Account[cite: 17].

question_html: If net profit before charging manager's commission is ₹2,00,000 and the manager is entitled to a commission of 10% on net profit *after* charging such commission, what is the amount of commission?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Commission after charging = $ ext{Net Profit} imes rac{ ext{Rate}}{100 + ext{Rate}} = 2,00,000 imes rac{10}{110} = ext{₹}18,181.82$ (approx ₹18,182)[cite: 17].

question_html: Sengupta & Co. employs a team of 8 workers paid ₹33,000 per month each starting April 1, 2021. Salaries are paid on the first working day of every month, one month in arrears. What is the total salary charged to Profit and Loss Account for the year ended 31st March, 2022?
answer_html: Answer: (A) For 8 employees for full year at ₹33,000 p.m., total salary charged = $8 imes 33,000 imes 12 = ext{₹}31,68,000$ (without trainees)[cite: 17].

question_html: Mr. Kotriwal had advance subscription from customers of ₹2,00,000 on 1.4.2021 (of which ₹1,500,000... wait, text says ₹1,50,000 is related to 2021-22). During 2021-22 he made cash sales of ₹5,00,000. If closing balance of advance is ₹1,70,000, what is total money received during the year?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total money received = Cash sales during the year (₹5,00,000) + Advance received during the year (₹1,20,000 balancing figure) = ₹6,20,000[cite: 17].

question_html: In an excerpt of a trading & P&L account where Cost of Goods Sold is ₹45,00,000, Sales is ₹1,00,00,000, rent is ₹26,00,000, office expenses is ₹13,00,000, manager's commission is 10% on net profit before charging such commission (amounting to ₹2,00,000), what is the Gross Profit?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Gross Profit = Sales ($1,00,00,000) - COGS ($45,00,000) = ₹55,00,000[cite: 17].

question_html: If opening inventory is ₹1,00,000, net purchases are ₹6,00,000, direct expenses are ₹80,000, and closing inventory is ₹2,00,000, what is the Cost of Goods Sold?
answer_html: Answer: (B) COGS = Opening Inventory ($1,00,000) + Net Purchases ($6,00,000) + Direct Expenses ($80,000) - Closing Inventory ($2,00,000) = ₹5,80,000[cite: 17].

question_html: When goods are distributed as free samples, how should the entry be recorded?

options.A: Debit Sales Account and Credit Purchases Account
options.B: Debit Free Samples / Advertisement Account and Credit Purchases Account
options.C: Debit Drawings Account and Credit Cash Account
options.D: Debit P&L Account and Credit Closing Stock

answer_html: Answer: (B) When goods are distributed as free samples, Free Samples / Advertisement Account is debited and Purchases Account is credited[cite: 17].

question_html: If a machine is purchased and wages paid for its installation are wrongly debited to the Wages Account instead of the Asset Account, what is the rectifying entry?

options.A: Debit Wages Account, Credit Machinery Account
options.B: Debit Machinery Account, Credit Wages Account
options.C: Debit Cash Account, Credit Machinery Account
options.D: Debit Capital Account, Credit Wages Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Wages paid for installation of a fixed asset should be added to the cost of the asset; the rectifying entry is to debit Plant and Machinery Account and credit Wages Account[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following items fromCrimpson Traders' P&L account represents a transfer to provisions?

options.A: Retained profit for the year
options.B: Bad debts written off
options.C: Increase in provision for doubtful debts
options.D: None of the above

answer_html: Answer: (C) Depreciation, increase in provision for doubtful debts, and liability for tax represent transfers to provisions[cite: 17].

question_html: When arranging assets in the Balance Sheet under the 'Permanence' approach, which assets are presented first?

options.A: Cash in hand and cash at bank
options.B: Trade receivables and short-term investments
options.C: Assets that are to be used for the long term and are not meant to be sold, such as Land and Building
options.D: Inventories in trade

answer_html: Answer: (C) Under the Permanence approach, assets which are to be used for long term in the business and are not meant to be sold (fixed assets) are presented first[cite: 17].

question_html: If insurance premium of ₹55,000 includes ₹40,000 paid towards proprietor's life insurance policy and the balance covers the period from 1.4.2021 to 30.6.2022 (15 months), what is the amount transferred to the Profit and Loss Account?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Personal premium (₹40,000) is deducted. Balance business insurance = ₹15,000 for 15 months. Prepaid for 3 months = ₹3,000. Amount transferred to P&L = $15,000 - 3,000 = ext{₹}12,000$[cite: 17].

question_html: When preparing the opening entry for a new accounting period, what accounts are credited?

options.A: All asset accounts
options.B: All liability accounts and the capital account
options.C: Trading account and Profit & Loss account
options.D: Cash account and bank account

answer_html: Answer: (B) In the opening entry, the assets shown in the balance sheet are debited and the liabilities and the capital account are credited[cite: 17].

question_html: If Sundry Debtors include ₹20,000 due from Robert and Sundry Creditors include ₹10,000 due to Robert, how is this handled when creating a provision for doubtful debts of 5%?

options.A: Provision is calculated on gross debtors without adjusting Robert's balance.
options.B: Robert's credit balance is cancelled against his debit balance, and provision is calculated on the adjusted debtors balance.
options.C: Robert's balance is added to total creditors.
options.D: No provision is calculated on debtors.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Robert's balance is cancelled/adjusted against sundry creditors, and the adjusted balance of sundry debtors is used to calculate the provision for doubtful debts[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the effect of a decrease in the provision for doubtful debts on net profit?

options.A: An increase in net profit
options.B: A decrease in net profit
options.C: No effect on net profit
options.D: An increase in liabilities

answer_html: Answer: (A) A decrease in the provision for doubtful debts results in a credit to the P&L account, thereby causing an increase in net profit[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following describes the correct treatment of goods returned by customers on 31st March, valued at ₹15,000, which were included in closing stock but for which no entry was passed?

options.A: Deduct from sales and deduct from sundry debtors
options.B: Add to sales and add to sundry debtors
options.C: Ignore since they are already in stock
options.D: Debit purchases and credit cash

answer_html: Answer: (A) Goods returned by customers should be deducted from sales and deducted from sundry debtors (trade receivables)[cite: 17].

question_html: When purchases include the purchase of a fixed asset (e.g. furniture for ₹10,000), what adjustment is required in the final accounts?

options.A: Deduct ₹10,000 from purchases and add ₹10,000 to the furniture asset account
options.B: Add ₹10,000 to purchases and deduct from furniture
options.C: Leave purchases as is and debit P&L account
options.D: Ignore the error

answer_html: Answer: (A) Capital expenditure wrongly included in revenue purchases must be deducted from purchases and added to the respective asset account[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the accounting entry for writing off bad debts when a provision for doubtful debts already exists?

options.A: Debit Provision for Bad Debts Account, Credit Bad Debts Account
options.B: Debit Bad Debts Account, Credit Customer's Account
options.C: Debit Profit and Loss Account, Credit Provision for Doubtful Debts Account
options.D: Debit Sales Account, Credit Bad Debts Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bad debts are written off by debiting Bad Debts Account and crediting Customer's Account, which are then absorbed by the provision[cite: 17].

question_html: How should bank overdraft secured against hypothecation of stock be reported if the bank overdraft is 80% of the real value of stock (after a 20% margin)?

options.A: Stock is valued at 100% of real value and shown as current asset, while overdraft is shown as liability.
options.B: Stock is ignored completely.
options.C: Overdraft is deducted from cash.
options.D: Stock is shown on the liabilities side.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The full real value of closing stock is shown as an asset in the Balance Sheet, and the bank overdraft is shown as a liability[cite: 17].

question_html: If goods are withdrawn by the proprietor for personal use, how is it recorded?

options.A: Debited to Sales Account and credited to Capital Account
options.B: Subtracted from Purchases Account and debited to Drawings Account (or Capital Account)
options.C: Debited to P&L Account as an expense
options.D: Added to Purchases and added to Capital

answer_html: Answer: (B) Goods used for personal use are subtracted from Purchases Account and debited to Drawings / Capital Account[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the sequence of the accounting cycle?

options.A: Final accounts -> Trial balance -> Ledger -> Journal
options.B: Journalising -> Posting to ledger -> Trial balance -> Income statement -> Balance sheet
options.C: Balance sheet -> Trial balance -> Journal -> Ledger
options.D: Trial balance -> Final accounts -> Journal -> Ledger

answer_html: Answer: (B) The accounting cycle proceeds in this order: recording transactions in journal, posting to ledger, trial balance, trading and profit and loss account, and balance sheet[cite: 17].

question_html: When a steel table purchased for ₹14,000 is sold for the same price, but the sale proceeds were wrongly credited to the Sales Account instead of the Furniture Account, what is the correct adjustment?

options.A: Deduct ₹14,000 from Sales Account and reduce Furniture asset by ₹14,000
options.B: Add ₹14,000 to Sales and add to Furniture
options.C: Ignore since there is no profit or loss
options.D: Debit Cash and Credit Capital

answer_html: Answer: (A) Sale of furniture incorrectly credited to sales must be deducted from Sales Account and deducted from the Furniture asset account[cite: 17].

question_html: If a loan from Viswanath of ₹3,00,000 was taken on 1.5.2021 at 12% per annum, and interest paid as per trial balance is ₹27,000, what is the outstanding interest on loan at the end of the year (31st March, 2022)?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest accrued for 11 months (from May 1 to March 31) = $3,00,000 imes 12\% imes (11/12) = ext{₹}33,000$. Less interest paid as per trial balance (₹27,000) = Outstanding interest of ₹6,000[cite: 17].

question_html: How is input CGST and input SGST utilized against output IGST?

options.A: Input tax credits are ignored in final accounts.
options.B: Output IGST liability is paid by utilizing input CGST and input SGST first, and any remaining input balance is reported as an asset in the Balance Sheet.
options.C: Input CGST and SGST are debited to Profit and Loss Account as expenses.
options.D: They are added to trade payables.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Output IGST is paid by utilizing input CGST and SGST, and any closing balance of input tax credit is reported as an asset in the Balance Sheet[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following items is considered an abnormal loss and debited to the Profit and Loss Account?

options.A: Normal evaporation of liquids in stock
options.B: Loss of property by fire to the extent not covered by insurance
options.C: Regular depreciation of machinery
options.D: Trade discount allowed to customers

answer_html: Answer: (B) Loss resulting from fire or accident to the extent not covered by insurance must be debited to the Profit and Loss Account[cite: 17].

question_html: If purchases include sales return of ₹2,575 and sales include purchases return of ₹1,725, what rectifying entries are required?

options.A: Debit Returns Inward A/c and Sales A/c, Credit Purchases A/c and Returns Outward A/c
options.B: Debit Purchases A/c, Credit Sales A/c
options.C: No adjustment is necessary
options.D: Debit Cash A/c, Credit Capital A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Returns inward and sales return incorrectly mixed with purchases must be rectified by debiting Returns Inward and Sales, and crediting Purchases and Returns Outward[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the purpose of maintaining Bills Receivable and Bills Payable Books?

options.A: To record daily weather updates
options.B: To act as journals (Day Books) recording details of bills in chronological order
options.C: To calculate income tax returns
options.D: To record physical stock counts

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bills receivable and bills payable books are journals (Day Books) maintained to record details of bills receivable and payable in chronological order[cite: 17].

question_html: How are provisions appearing in the Balance Sheet presented on the liability side or asset side?

options.A: Provision for Bad Debts and Provision for Depreciation are shown as separate liabilities without any deduction.
options.B: Provision for Bad Debts and Provision for Discount are deducted from trade receivables, while Provision for Depreciation is deducted from the respective asset.
options.C: All provisions are added to capital.
options.D: All provisions are ignored in the Balance Sheet.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Provision for Bad Debts and Discount are deducted from total book debts, and Provision for Depreciation is deducted from the cost of the assets concerned[cite: 17].

question_html: Why does the Balance Sheet have equal totals on both sides (Assets equal to Capital plus Liabilities)?

options.A: Because of the dual aspect concept where capital equals the difference between total assets and total liabilities.
options.B: Because trial balance totals are artificially forced to match.
options.C: Because revenues always equal expenses.
options.D: Because cash in hand must equal bank overdraft.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Since capital always equals the difference between assets and liabilities and the capital account arrives at this figure, the two sides of the Balance Sheet must have the same totals[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the effect on net profit if outstanding expenses are omitted from being adjusted at the end of the accounting period?

options.A: Net profit is understated
options.B: Net profit is overstated
options.C: Net profit remains unaffected
options.D: Gross profit becomes zero

answer_html: Answer: (B) Omitting outstanding expenses means expenses are understated, which leads to an overstatement of net profit[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following expenditures is considered an exception to the rule that only costs expected to yield revenue should be debited to the Profit and Loss Account?

options.A: Normal purchases of trading goods
options.B: Loss resulting from property damaged by fire not covered by insurance
options.C: Carriage inwards on purchases
options.D: Wages paid to godown workers

answer_html: Answer: (B) Losses resulting from fire damage (not covered by insurance), falling selling prices, or bad debts are exceptions that must be debited to the P&L account to prevent overstating profit[cite: 17].
